solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boss's mistake? Right

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the boss has blundered, and is told yes, correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Boss is a link meaning 'is'; the question mark hints that 'mistake? Right' is not a dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British synonym: a gaffer is the person in charge, a foreman or manager.

clue.text: This can be elevating or a bore

definitions.meaning: the envelope of a balloon or airship holds lifting gas and raises the craft
a tedious person who talks too much

explanation.surface: A riddle: something that might lift you up or else weary you.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas-filled bag lifts a balloon; colloquially a windbag who talks endlessly is tiresome company.

clue.text: Stew faces sir worse for wear, in need of energy

indicators.note: something worse for wear is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dishevelled gentleman's face looks tired and he needs a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worse for wear' rearranges FACES SIR into FRICASSE, and 'in need of' attaches E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of meat cut up and cooked in a white sauce, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Confront European once you get wound up?

parts.note: ye is the old form of 'you', used once upon a time
yarn wound up forms a ball

explanation.surface: A European is challenged, perhaps once someone becomes agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like 'angry' but means coiled into a ball; 'once' marks the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare them down at close range, facing them directly.

clue.text: Educated version of 'speed of light'?

parts.note: lite is the commercial spelling of light, as on low-calorie products
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A learned rendering of the physicist's phrase 'speed of light'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed of light' read as a phrase becomes rate of lite, i.e. LITE then RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able to read and write, well-read, is educated.

clue.text: Rider's position is then terribly bad

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled, so is then is rearranged

parts.note: addle describes an egg gone rotten, i.e. bad

explanation.surface: A horseman's situation is described as dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' shuffles IS THEN to INTHES; 'bad' gives ADDLE as in an addled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally where a horseman sits; idiomatically, being in control.

clue.text: Before child becomes recluse

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
a mite is an affectionate word for a small child

explanation.surface: Before reaching adulthood, a youngster withdraws from society.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit, especially a religious one, living apart from society.

clue.text: Spiritual position when one meets one

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a likewise means one

explanation.surface: A meditative stance adopted when two people come together.
explanation.definitionFit: A posture held in yoga, a practice with spiritual roots.

clue.text: The Spanish fixture's hot for the last man in?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a sporting fixture is an event
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A Spanish match is heating up for the final batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each side has eleven batsmen; the final one to go in is number 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal example: in a cricket batting order of eleven, the final batsman bats in that position.

clue.text: Naughty wives left to go swinging

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters of wives run wild

explanation.surface: Mischievous wives depart for some partner-swapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges WIVES to SWIVE, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot round, turning on a fixed point, is to move swinging about.

clue.text: Cheapest classes of ox get old

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but the word names the cheap part of a ship collectively

parts.note: a steer is a castrated ox
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Low-grade cattle that are past their best.
explanation.definitionFit: On passenger ships, the lowest-fare accommodation for travellers, historically near the rudder.

clue.text: Fall of molten rock flowing over in Italy too

indicators.note: flowing over suggests turning over, so the word for molten rock runs backwards

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano
anche is Italian for too or also

explanation.surface: A volcanic eruption in Italy, perhaps Etna, sends lava pouring down.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow or rock sliding down a mountainside is a great fall.

clue.text: Nautical goo could be forming a clot

indicators.note: could be signals the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Slimy marine gunk may be congealing into a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of a liquid such as blood thickening into a solid mass.

clue.text: Presentation of international sorcerer

parts.note: a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A global conjuror puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Public image is how something is presented to others, its projected appearance.

clue.text: Jumping fleas found on foot soldiers — time for sackcloth and ashes

indicators.note: jumping fleas leap about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Fleas leaping onto infantry make it time for penitence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing sackcloth and ashes is the biblical show of humility and penitence, humbling oneself.

clue.text: Primitive man let eel wriggle

indicators.note: an eel wriggling twists about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An early human lets an eel squirm free.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and fundamental, of the raw forces of nature, hence primitive.

clue.text: Fish always found surrounded by fungus

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the word for always inside the fungus

parts.note: a morel is an edible fungus
aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A fish that is invariably encased in fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory snake-like marine creature of warm reefs, a type of fish.

clue.text: A cakewalk perhaps following almost public excess?

indicators.note: following puts the cake dance after the shortened word
almost means the word for public is used without its final letter

parts.note: overt means open or public
a cakewalk is an example of a dance, playfully read as a cake (bun) dance

explanation.surface: Is an easy win, coming after near-public exposure, a step too far?
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims OVERT to OVER; 'cakewalk' is a dance whose name is read as bun dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A superfluity, more than is needed, is an excess.

clue.text: Wind beginning to enter grave

parts.note: Auster is the south wind of classical myth

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of enter is taken

explanation.surface: A breeze starts to blow into a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and serious in manner, stern and solemn.

clue.text: Fertiliser salt's upset in dark, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by sound

parts.note: angry (irate) at night, read as night irate

explanation.surface: A chemical fertiliser is said to be disturbed in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Night (dark) plus irate (upset), spoken together, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salts of nitric acid, such as ammonium compounds, are widely used as fertilisers.

clue.text: View of a risky investment taking time

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a risky investment

explanation.surface: An opinion on a gamble in shares that needs time to pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook or prospect from a place; also a particular way of viewing things.

clue.text: Voices heard in maelstrom, odd parts obscured by start of snow

indicators.note: hiding the odd-numbered letters leaves the even ones of maelstrom
start of means the first letter of snow is taken

explanation.surface: Singers are heard in a whirling storm, partly muffled by falling snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts obscured' removes the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of MAELSTROM, leaving ALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing parts, plural: lower female or high male voices in a choir.

clue.text: God's point or spike

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N (north) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Is this the sharp end of a deity's weapon, or a spike?
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp prickle on a stem is a natural spike.

clue.text: A point about small part of business is complete skill

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: a ness is a headland or promontory, a point
dept is the abbreviation for a department, one part of a business

explanation.surface: A detail of company affairs shows thorough competence.
explanation.walkthrough: A and NESS go 'about' DEPT, with the abbreviation sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Proficiency or expertise; being thoroughly expert is having full mastery.

clue.text: Obscure Tories ruined in City

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the City abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of Tories are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Little-known Conservatives come to grief in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' makes SOTERI from TORIES, set 'in' EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Understood by only a few initiates, hence hard to grasp.

clue.text: Amount of power the French male twigs

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the word names interwoven twigs as a material

parts.note: a watt is a unit measuring power
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A French man's twigs supply a unit of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rods and branches interlaced to make fences and walls, as in wattle and daub.

clue.text: Organ, say, is restricting in making a jab

parts.note: a lung is a bodily organ

indicators.note: restricting means the abbreviation hems in the other word

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means

explanation.surface: A body part is said to be constricted when an injection is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a jab' is a fencing or boxing thrust, not an injection as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusting forward, as a fencer does, is delivering a jab.

clue.text: From sea to river for French variety of grape

parts.note: mer is French for sea
the Lot is a river in southern France

explanation.surface: A journey through France, from coast to waterway, ends up with wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A black wine grape originating in Bordeaux, a widely grown red cultivar.
